title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
content_md: LaLiga, Spain's top men's professional football league, disclosed a data breach that exposed personal information belonging to users of its services and those of some affiliated clubs. According to the organization, the incident occurred between November 14 and 16, and the attacker extracted data from compromised systems. LaLiga organizes Spain’s top two men’s professional football divisions. The top league is one of the world’s most prominent football leagues, where clubs with a global audience, such as Real Madrid, FC Barcelona, and Atlético Madrid, play. On November 16, the organization’s security team identified the source of the unauthorized access and implemented measures to block the attack and stop the data extraction. “LALIGA was the target of a cyberattack on one of its technology platforms for fan services,” reads the announcement . “Between November 14 and 16, a cybercriminal gained unauthorized access to the platform and extracted personal data belonging to users registered for digital services offered by LALIGA and some clubs.” LaLiga underlined that the incident was confined to a specific platform and did not extend to other systems that support the running of the competitions. After implementing containment measures, LaLiga launched an investigation to determine the scope of the incident and introduced more thorough monitoring to detect future attempts to breach its systems.
